families.name: definition
families.label: Double or cryptic definition
families.blurb: No wordplay at all: the answer is not built from any of the clue's letters. It is two definitions placed together, or one playful, misleading description of the answer.

families.name: and_lit
families.label: &lit
families.blurb: &lit is short for “and literally so”. The whole clue does double duty: read it once as a definition, then read the very same words again as wordplay.

families.name: anagram
families.label: Anagram
families.blurb: Letters handed to you in the clue get shuffled into the answer. Find those letters and check they add up to the number in brackets.

families.name: homophone
families.label: Homophone
families.blurb: The wordplay describes how the answer sounds rather than how it is spelled.

families.name: charade
families.label: Charade
families.blurb: The answer is built from pieces laid end to end, each clued separately — read the wordplay left to right.

families.name: change
families.label: Container, reversal or deletion
families.blurb: A piece of the wordplay is changed, not just placed next to the others: it is put inside something, turned around, or trimmed.

families.name: selection
families.label: Hidden or letter selection
families.blurb: The answer's letters are already sitting in the clue in order — the job is working out which ones to pick out.

types.name: anagram
types.label: anagram
types.blurb: An anagram: the letters of some words in the clue are rearranged to make the answer. Find the indicator, then check those letters add up to the number in brackets.

types.name: charade
types.label: charade
types.blurb: A charade: the answer is built from parts placed one after another, each clued separately.

types.name: container
types.label: container
types.blurb: A container: one part is placed inside another. Look for words like holding, in, covering, swallowing.

types.name: hidden_word
types.label: hidden word
types.blurb: A hidden word: the answer is spelled out, letter by letter in order, inside the words of the clue.

types.name: homophone
types.label: homophone
types.blurb: A homophone: the wordplay describes something that sounds like the answer.

types.name: reversal
types.label: reversal
types.blurb: A reversal: something is spelled backwards (in a down clue, words meaning 'up' can signal this).

types.name: deletion
types.label: deletion
types.blurb: A deletion: letters are removed from a longer word — heads, tails or insides.

types.name: double_definition
types.label: double definition
types.blurb: A double definition: two definitions sit side by side; there is no other wordplay.

types.name: cryptic_definition
types.label: cryptic definition
types.blurb: A cryptic definition: there is no separate wordplay — the whole clue is one playful, misleading description of the answer.

types.name: and_lit
types.label: &lit
types.blurb: An &lit (short for “and literally so”): the whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay at once.

types.name: spoonerism
types.label: spoonerism
types.blurb: A spoonerism: swap the opening sounds of two words to get the answer.

types.name: cycling
types.label: cycling
types.blurb: Cycling: letters move from one end to the other without changing their order — the word rotates rather than shuffles.

types.name: substitution
types.label: substitution
types.blurb: A substitution: one indicated letter or chunk stands in for another — make the swap and the answer appears.

types.name: palindrome
types.label: palindrome
types.blurb: A palindrome: the answer reads the same forwards and backwards, and that symmetry is the wordplay — there is nothing else to take apart.

types.name: letter_selection
types.label: letter selection
types.blurb: Letter selection: keep only some letters of the indicated word(s) — the first, the last, the middle, the outside, every other one, or the one at a counted position — and throw the rest away.
